A mature medium-large powerful agile American Leopard Hound, body slightly longer than tall, broad strong level back, muscular slightly arched short loin, deep well-sprung chest to elbow and mild tuck. Proportionate broad flat skull and medium heavy muzzle slightly shorter than skull, definite stop, tight dark lips, black nose and brown nearly round eyes. High-set short-to-medium broad-based natural drop ears. Strong straight round-boned forelegs, well-muscled balanced hindquarters with bent stifles and low hocks; compact arched-toed cat-like paws. Dense close-fitting smooth double coat, rough outer hairs and fine undercoat. Blue-grey or mouse leopard mottling with independently arranged dark patches and restrained rust trim, very little white, never more than one third white. A complete natural long tail set low, carried relaxed in a shallow down/back curve with its free endpoint clear; no cropped ears or docked stump.

Independently arrange leopard patches; do not copy a researched dog, exact markings, tree-bracing stance or gallery framing. profileEvidence.summary: Eager to please and persistent on a scent, the American Leopard Hound is an all-purpose tree dog with a long working stride. It can follow an old track while remaining responsive to its handler’s voice, then hold game at bay. The UKC first recognized it as the Leopard Cur in 1998; its current name followed in 2008.
profileEvidence.shortDescription: An eager-to-please tree dog with a persistent nose, able to follow an old track and hold game at bay.
